findings.message: Scope in requires overriding `MergeQueue._rebase(candidate)` in merge.py. It must capture the pre-rebase head inside the serial slot and delegate to `super()._rebase(candidate)`. That private method belongs to squatch/mergequeue.py, which is not in Context. None of the Context tests (test_mergequeue.py tests only `admit`, `next_rework`, `_slot` and `_rework`) shows that `_rebase` exists, what signature it has, or that it runs inside the slot. The merge.py excerpt shows only `Merge._rebase(stem, worktree, run_seq)`, which has a different signature. The ticket also calls `compose_merge_queue`, `Merge._regate` and `Merge._squash`, but those are cut off in the rendered merge.py, so the reference closure of the hooked seam cannot be traced.
findings.paved_road: Add squatch/mergequeue.py to Context as read-only evidence; section 20 allows predecessor surfaces and it stays outside the fence. Then state the override against the real `_rebase` signature and serial-slot placement. Also make sure the part of merge.py that defines `compose_merge_queue`, `compose_pipeline`, `_regate` and `_squash` fits in the render (current 104238 chars against a 120000 headroom limit). If `_rebase` is not a stable hook, capture the head in the regate adapter's pre-rebase path instead.

findings.message: The fourth acceptance criterion says tests/test_daemon_composition.py proves two things that live in tests/test_mergequeue.py: that the literal `not hasattr(pipeline, "merge_queue")` assertion was migrated in `test_additive_composition_hook_does_not_change_phase1_composition`, and that `test_mergequeue_has_no_scheduler_or_watcher_dependency` is preserved. A test in one file cannot prove edits to another file, so the criterion names the wrong proof site. The first criterion's claim that tests prove `Merge.admit` and `Pipeline.run` 'remain unchanged' also has no mechanical observable.
findings.paved_road: Move the migration and preservation clauses into the tests/test_mergequeue.py criterion. Limit the test_daemon_composition.py criterion to the in-process `__main__` factory/Runner composition exposing `isinstance(pipeline.merge_queue, MergeQueue)` and preserving the existing dispatch/config and no-`serve` contracts. Rewrite 'unchanged' as a scope-out constraint, or as an observable behavior such as the existing admit tests still passing.

findings.message: The ownership record gives background-consumers two boundaries: the watcher/merge/box task lifetimes (tests/test_daemon_tasks.py) and the initial typed control inbox (squatch/control.py, tests/test_control.py). control-inbox is left with `owns: []` and only hooks those files. Section 20 splits the pair differently. background-consumers owns the watcher, merge and box tasks. control-inbox owns the crash-safe, identity-bound, exactly-once, decision-journaled-before-mutation request intake, and it states that one ticket owns one independently provable boundary. As written, background-consumers cannot be proved on its task lifetimes alone. control-inbox also becomes a seed that only hooks files and owns no module, even though the registry names it as the owner of control.py. Your own Definition of rejected covers this: 'either boundary cannot be proved independently'.
findings.paved_road: Change the ownership record. background-consumers owns tests/test_daemon_tasks.py and hooks squatch/daemon.py. control-inbox owns squatch/control.py and tests/test_control.py and hooks squatch/daemon.py and tests/test_daemon_tasks.py, which keeps predecessor-test closure. Move the typed-inbox construction wording out of the background-consumers scope and into control-inbox. Update the matching ownership, fence and NEW_AT_AUTHORING owner assertions in tests/test_seeded_phase3_07.py. The Context map, suffix lists and budgets stay the same.
